blocks.text: The challenge of bug reporting documentation

Digital product testers often struggle with the sheer volume of documentation required. Between reproducing bugs and logging them in Jira, your day fills up fast. You might spend hours moving between VS Code, Postman, and your browser. This creates a fragmented workflow. Every time you switch apps to write a report, you lose momentum. Clear bug reporting documentation is the backbone of a successful release. If your steps to reproduce are unclear, developers will bounce the ticket back to you. This wastes time for everyone involved.
How Lazur helps with bug reporting documentation

Lazur works by listening to your voice and observing your screen only when you tell it to. Hold the ⌥ ⌘ keys to ask a question about what you see. If you are stuck on a specific error in your browser, ask Lazur to explain it. It does not click buttons for you, but it can point at the exact element you need to look at. This helps when you are documenting a UI bug. You can then use the fn key to dictate the steps to reproduce directly into your bug tracking software.

blocks.text: Managing your time as a digital product tester

The average knowledge worker receives 121 emails per day. For a tester, this is a major distraction. Every time you pause to check an email, you need over 23 minutes to get back to your testing flow. Lazur helps you manage this by drafting quick replies or summaries. You can ask Lazur to draft a response while you keep your eyes on the screen. This keeps you in the zone.

Many testers write reports that are too vague. They forget to include environment details or specific version numbers. If you are testing on macOS, always note your version. If you are using Chrome, note if you have specific extensions running. Lazur can help you remember these details. Ask it to look at your system info and draft a summary for your report. This saves you from hunting through System Settings manually.
Always verify that your bug reports do not contain sensitive user data. Follow your company's security policies strictly when documenting issues.
blocks.title: Keep it secure

blocks.text: Tools for the modern tester on Mac

Your Mac setup likely includes tools like iTerm2, Docker Desktop, and GitHub Desktop. These are essential for modern testing. When you run into a command line error, you can hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur to explain the output. This is faster than searching through documentation pages. It gives you a quick answer right where you are working.

Voice dictation is a powerful way to speed up your documentation. When you hold the fn key, you can talk to your computer. Lazur turns your speech into clean text. This is perfect for writing long descriptions of bug behavior. You can talk naturally, and the text appears at your cursor. It is much faster than typing out long paragraphs while you are trying to remember what you just saw in the app.

faq.question: Does Lazur work with Jira or Notion?
faq.answer: Lazur works in any app that accepts text. You can use it to dictate or draft content into Jira, Notion, or any other web-based tool you use for documentation.

faq.question: Is my data private when using Lazur?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur only listens and looks at your screen while you hold the shortcut. The data is sent to AI providers to answer your request and is not stored or used to train models.

faq.question: Can Lazur click buttons in my testing apps?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or operate other apps for you. It can point at elements on your screen, but you remain in control of all actions.
